text:
Toronto and Edmonton both arrive on three-game winning streaks, each from a wild finish two days ago. The Maple Leafs beat the Rangers 5-4 on Troy Stecher's goal with 0:28 left, and they're missing John Tavares (lower body), with Colton Sissons moving beside Nylander and McKenna. The Oilers came back from two goals down to beat Carolina 6-5 in a shootout, a night Nikolaj Ehlers reached 600 career points. They're without Mattias Ekholm, and Jake Walman is next in line for his minutes. The extra hook is Jack Roslovic, facing the team he scored 36 points for last season.

On chances, neither side has been dominant at five on five: TOR has taken 44% of the expected goals (the quality of shots) and EDM 49%. Our model has EDM slightly ahead tonight, 3.32 expected goals to 3.00. Edmonton's power play and penalty kill both grade out better, and Toronto's 4.1 penalties a game hand opponents chances. In net, projected starters Anthony Stolarz (TOR) and Tristan Jarry (EDM) are both below expected last season by goals saved above expected, which measures saves beyond what shot quality predicts: -6.6 for Stolarz, -4.2 for Jarry. This year Stolarz is +0.5 and Jarry -3.1.

Connor McDavid brings a 10-game point streak and we give him a 94% chance at a point. Leon Draisaitl has scored in five straight, at 46% to score tonight. Auston Matthews, two points from 800, sits at 37% to score. Our under-the-radar pick is Colton Dach, a third-line Oiler whose shots have been dangerous: 1.3 expected goals in his last six games. We put him at 14% to score, a player to watch.
